assumptions.choice: Initial and reinvestment grid orders are placed 1% away from the reference price (current close for the initial grid, last fill price for reinvestment steps)
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'a certain distance from the current price' without a number; 1% is the bench convention for an unstated grid spacing and reuses the spec's own trailing-entry example threshold context.

assumptions.choice: 0.5% from the volume-weighted average entry price
assumptions.reason: Directly matches the spec's own example ('e.g., 0.5% from the averaged entry price').
Spec says this is 'set by the user' but gives no value; chose a minimal concrete size so the doubling sequence (1,2,4,8,16,32) stays implementable within the fixed $10,000 starting cash.

assumptions.choice: Enabled: grid sell orders open short positions, grid buy orders open long positions
assumptions.reason: Spec explicitly requires 'a grid of limit buy and sell orders' for a perpetual-futures contrarian market maker, i.e. entries in both directions, which overrides the bench's long-only default.

assumptions.choice: Enabled: reinvestment orders add to an open position in the same direction while it is losing
assumptions.reason: This is the core Martingale mechanic the spec explicitly describes, overriding the bench's default of one position with no re-entry.

assumptions.choice: Not modeled; only one directional grid (long or short) is active at a time. When either side of the initial grid fills, the opposite pending order is canceled, and after the position fully closes via take-profit both sides are re-armed
assumptions.reason: infeasible — backtrader's default broker maintains a single netted position per data feed, so true simultaneous long and short exposure ('hedge mode') on one instrument cannot be represented; this is the closest literal reading that preserves the grid's two-sided intent while respecting the netting model.

assumptions.choice: Not implemented; only the static grid + fixed take-profit method (the spec's own base description) is used
assumptions.reason: infeasible — the spec labels both trailing features as optional alternatives ('can use'), and they require tracking retracement from intrabar extremes / order-book depth that is not derivable from daily OHLCV bars; the static method is fully specified and chosen instead.

assumptions.choice: While flat, cancel and recreate both grid orders on every bar so they stay centered on the current close
assumptions.reason: Spec requires the strategy to 'automatically create and cancel limit orders to maintain the grid around the current price' but does not state a recentering frequency; per-bar recentering is the most literal reading given the bar-by-bar next() execution model.

assumptions.topic: behavior after max reinvestment level reached
assumptions.choice: No further reinvestment orders are placed once the cap (5) is hit; the take-profit order remains active and the position simply waits to close, with no forced stop-loss exit
assumptions.reason: Spec only requires a limit on the number/volume of reinvestments to cap risk; it does not state any forced-exit rule beyond that cap, so none was added.
